titre: Applying to the family court judge (JAF)
resume: Form Cerfa n° 11530, the list of documents (birth certificates less than 3 months old), the competent court in Réunion (Saint-Denis or Saint-Pierre), the €50 stamp and when it is not due.
aQuoiCaSert: The family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF) settles disagreements between parents about how parental authority is exercised, where the child lives, visiting and staying rights, or child support. The judge can also change an existing decision when circumstances change, or give court approval (homologation) to an agreement reached by the parents so that it has the force of a judgment. In Réunion, two courts (tribunaux judiciaires) handle these cases: Saint-Denis and Saint-Pierre.
quiEstConcerne: Parents, married or not, who cannot reach an agreement about their children.
A parent who wants an existing decision changed (moving house, change in income, new arrangements).
Parents who agree with each other and want their parenting agreement (convention parentale) approved by the court.
A parent who receives the ASF (allocation de soutien familial, family support allowance) with no child support set and must apply to the judge within 4 months.
aSavoir: Form: Cerfa n° 11530 "Demande au juge aux affaires familiales" (application to the family court judge), to fill in online or on paper. A fully online application is also possible.

Competent court: the one for the place where the parent the child usually lives with resides; if the parents still live together, the one for the family's place of residence. In Réunion: the tribunal judiciaire de Saint-Denis or de Saint-Pierre, depending on your municipality.

A lawyer is not mandatory before the family court judge (one is required on appeal). Legal aid (aide juridictionnelle) can cover the costs depending on your income: see the guide entry "Applying for legal aid (aide juridictionnelle)".

€50 tax stamp (timbre fiscal), electronic only, bought online by bank card before you apply. It is not due if you receive legal aid, for approval of a parenting agreement, or for a protection order. Valid for 12 months, refundable within 18 months if unused.

Prior mediation: the pilot scheme that required it at the Saint-Denis court before certain applications ended on December 31, 2024. It is still recommended, but no longer mandatory to apply to the judge.
Parents in agreement: joint application for approval of the parenting agreement (Cerfa n° 16139), signed by both.

Violence: a protection order (ordonnance de protection) is requested from the family court judge, with no prior police complaint required. The hearing takes place within 6 days of being scheduled. Immediate danger: 17 or 112. Helpline: 3919, free from Réunion, 24 hours a day.
This guide does not replace legal advice: for your situation, contact a lawyer or a point-justice (free legal information center).

documents.libelle: Form Cerfa n° 11530, completed, dated and signed
documents.detail: Original for the court, a copy for you. Can be filled in online on service-public.gouv.fr.

documents.libelle: Full copy (copie intégrale) of your birth certificate, less than 3 months old
documents.detail: Not an extract. Request it free of charge online on service-public.gouv.fr (see the guide entry "Getting a birth certificate").

documents.libelle: Full copy of the birth certificate of each child concerned, less than 3 months old
documents.detail: Same process, from the town hall (mairie) of the child's place of birth. Allow time for delivery, especially if the child was born in mainland France.

documents.libelle: Family record book (livret de famille) or full copy of the marriage certificate less than 3 months old

documents.detail: ID card or passport, front and back.

documents.libelle: Copy of previous judgments (divorce, separation, parental authority, child support)
documents.detail: If you no longer have it, ask the court registry (greffe) of the court that issued it for a copy.
Depending on your application: a bill, a rent receipt or a letter confirming you are housed by someone (attestation d'hébergement).

Especially if your application concerns child support: latest tax notice and income tax return, last 3 payslips, benefit statement from the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office), rent, loans, child-related costs.
Unless you have legal aid or are applying for approval of a parenting agreement.

documents.libelle: Legal aid decision or receipt of your application, if you applied for it

documents.detail: For example: school attendance certificate, written exchanges about arrangements, witness statements. Avoid documents unrelated to your application.

etapes.titre: First try to reach an amicable solution
etapes.detail: Family mediation or a written agreement to have approved. The form asks whether an amicable approach has been tried. No mediation in cases of violence.
They must be less than 3 months old when you file and arrive by post: they are often the document that delays the file.

etapes.titre: Fill in Cerfa n° 11530 or the online application
etapes.detail: Explain clearly what you are asking for (residence, visiting rights, amount of child support) and why.

etapes.titre: Buy the €50 stamp if you are not exempt
etapes.detail: Online, by bank card, before sending your application.

Signed Cerfa; full copies of birth certificates less than 3 months old (yours and each child's); family record book or marriage certificate; ID; previous judgments; proof of income if you mention child support; stamp or legal aid decision. Make a full copy.

etapes.titre: Send or hand in the file at the court registry of the competent court
etapes.detail: Saint-Denis or Saint-Pierre depending on where the child lives, or file the application online. Store the copy in the Court file section of your Vault.
You are informed of the date and the other parent is summoned by registered letter. Add it to the calendar with a reminder and bring the originals of your documents.

ou.detail: Open Monday to Friday, 7:45 a.m. to 12:15 p.m. and 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. Email: accueil.tj-st-denis-de-la-reunion@justice.fr.
28 rue Augustin Archambaud, 97410 Saint-Pierre. Open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 12 p.m. and 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.
Free legal information, help putting your file together and applying for legal aid.

ou.nom: Violences Femmes Info (violence against women helpline)
ou.detail: Listening and guidance, free and anonymous, 24 hours a day, including from Réunion. In immediate danger, call 17 or 112.

To be confirmed locally: the exact reception address of the tribunal judiciaire de Saint-Denis (the directory gives avenue Desbassyns, and 5 avenue André Malraux for the legal aid office).
To be confirmed locally: the role of the local courts (tribunaux de proximité) of Saint-Paul and Saint-Benoît in family cases, and average waiting times for a hearing.
